## Mathematical Description of Regularized Regression

NOTE TO SELF: All equations can be derived from the ESL textbook

This section examines the mathematical background for the regularized regression model types of: Ridge, Lasso, and Elastic-Net regression. All assume a model of the form (here, without interaction terms):
$$y = \beta_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_i x_i + \varepsilon.$$
Where the $\beta_i$s are found by solving (though specific instances introduce additional terms):
$$\min_\vec{\beta} \left\|  X\vec{\beta} - \vec{y} \right\|^2_2\text{, with } X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p} \text{ the design matrix}$$
The general solution is given (analytically) by:
$$\hat{\vec{\beta}} = \left(X^T X \right)^{-1} X^T\vec{y}$$
We now explain the various cases of regularization.

### Ridge Regression
The Ridge regression penalizes the size of the parameters with an L2 norm. Specifically the optimization problem is given by,
$$\min_{\vec{\beta}} \left\| X\vec{\beta} - \vec{y} \right\|_2^2 + \lambda \| \vec{\beta} \|_2^2$$

The analytical solution is given by:
$$ \vec{\beta} = \left(  X^TX + \lambda I \right)^{-1}X^T\vec{y} $$
Note that in the previous two equations, $\lambda$ is a hyperparameter that can be tuned with cross validation. We now proceed to Lasso Regression.

### Lasso Regression
The Lasso regression penalizes the size of the parameters with an L1 norm. The optimization problem is:
$$\min_{\vec{\beta}} \left\| X\vec{\beta} - \vec{y} \right\|_2^2 + \lambda \| \vec{\beta} \|_1$$
Since the L1 norm is not differentiable at $0$, there is no closed-form, analytical solution to the above problem. One can use solvers for convex problems capable of dealing with non-smooth objectives. The optimality condition is given by: 

$$
0 \in 2 X^\top (X \hat{\beta} - y) + \lambda\, \partial \|\hat{\beta}\|_1,
\quad
(\partial \|\hat{\beta}\|_1)_i =
\begin{cases}
\{1\}, & \hat{\beta}_i > 0,\\[1mm]
\{-1\}, & \hat{\beta}_i < 0,\\[1mm]
[-1,1], & \hat{\beta}_i = 0
\end{cases}
$$

Again, $\lambda$ is a hyperparameter that can be tuned with cross validation. We now move onto the generalization of the previous two regularization methods, elastic-net regression.

### Elastic-Net Regression
The elastic-net regression uses a convex combination of the lasso penalty (L1) and ridge penalty (L2). Specifically, the optimization problem is given by:
$$\min_{\vec{\beta}} \left\| X\vec{\beta} - \vec{y} \right\|_2^2 + \lambda \left( \left(1 - \alpha  \right) \| \vec{\beta} \|_1 + \alpha\|\vec{\beta}  \|_2^2 \right)$$

We again have the L1 norm which is not differentiable at $0$. Thereby a convex solver capable of optimizing non-smooth objectives should be used. The optimality condition is given by:
Since the L1 norm is not differentiable at $0$, there is no closed-form, analytical solution to the above problem. Once again solvers for convex problems capable of dealing with non-smooth objectives must be applied. The optimality condition is given by: 

$$
0 \in 2 X^\top (X \hat{\beta} - y) +  \lambda \left( 2 \alpha \hat{\vec{\beta}} + (1 - \alpha) \partial \|\hat{\beta}\|_1 \right),
\quad
(\partial \|\hat{\beta}\|_1)_i =
\begin{cases}
\{1\}, & \hat{\beta}_i > 0,\\[1mm]
\{-1\}, & \hat{\beta}_i < 0,\\[1mm]
[-1,1], & \hat{\beta}_i = 0
\end{cases}
$$

The parameters $\lambda$ and $\alpha$ are hyperparameters to be tuned via cross validation.
